classical

Plaut. Rud. 3.1.5 (Lewis & Short)

īnscītus, īnscīta, īnscītum

declension

ignorant, unskilful, silly

(vōx plērumque cōmica: Plaut.; rāra apud Cic.)

Lewis & Short: rare in Cicero.

Other words

  • indoctus, indocta, indoctum — uneducated, ignorant, untaught

    declension · classical · Cic. Brut. 178 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 331

  • īnscientia, īnscientiae f. — ignorance, inexperience

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Traupman 154; Cic. Sull. 40: in tantīs tenebrīs errōris et īnscientiae (Lewis & Short); Traupman 331

  • nesapius, nesapia, nesapium — ignoramus, fool

    declension · also used · classical · Petr. 50.5 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 331

    An adjective, “unwise”, in Petronius’ freedman’s talk; Traupman uses it as a noun.

See also stupid, education.
